title: Verdier axioms and stagewise triangulation
statement:
The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this verification: the four
axioms verified here are exactly Stacks Project, Derived Categories,
Definition 13.3.2 ([Tag 0145](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0145),
fetched and quoted: "the definition of a triangulated category as given in
Verdier's thesis", an additive category with an additive auto-equivalence
$[1]$ and a set of distinguished triangles subject to TR1--TR4, TR4 being
the octahedral axiom); the triangles and their morphisms are Definition
13.3.1 ([Tag 0144](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0144)) and the exact
functors of the last sentence are Definition 13.3.3 ([Tag
014V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014V)). The closest verification
of the axioms in Stacks for a category that is constructed rather than
assumed is Proposition 13.5.6 ([Tag
05R6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R6)), which proves TR1--TR4 for
a localization $S^{-1}\mathcal D$ whose distinguished triangles are by
definition the images of distinguished triangles of $\mathcal D$, and Lemma
13.4.15 ([Tag 014C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014C)) is the
normal form for TR4. The blueprint adds the verification for the triangles
of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones] together with the exactness of the
finite-stage inclusions $j_E$.

proof.text: Use the coefficient and scheme hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. For a finite extension $E$, set $A=\mathcal O_E$. Its constant sections in each $(A/\varpi^n)_T$ form a compatible family, hence define $A\to\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_T)$ for the actual limit sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. On the abelian category of $A_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], define $(a f)_U(x)=a_U f_U(x)$. Commutativity of $A_T(U)$ makes this an $A_T(U)$-linear map; compatibility of constant sections with restrictions makes it a sheaf map. The module laws and bilinear composition hold sectionwise. Apply [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] with the ordinary ring $A$ to obtain $A$-linear Hom groups and $A$-linear shifts on $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$. The full integral compatible uniform tower subcategory inherits these Hom groups and actions.

source.place: Implicit finite-stage input: linearity of the completed-coefficient derived category.

proof.text: For each finite $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] makes the integral compatible uniform tower category triangulated under the stated noetherian, finite-dimensional and $\ell$-invertible hypotheses. Step 1 supplies its $\mathcal O_E$-linear structure and linear shift. Apply [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] with $R=\mathcal O_E$ and its uniformizer $\varpi$. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], this raw scalar localization is exactly $\mathcal C_E(T)$. Thus the four finite-stage axioms of [def-weil-triangulated-category] apply. The transition functors are exact with the coherent associators and shift comparisons specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

source.place: Implicit finite-stage TR1--TR4 inputs for all four axiom sentences.

proof.text:
The category and shift are additive by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. The inclusion $j_E$ sends a map $v$ to $[E,v]$, so it is additive by the common-stage addition formula. For $E\subseteq M$ define $\rho_{M/E,K}:(E,K)\to(M,T_{M/E}K)$ and its inverse by the identity representative over $M$. Both composites are identity representatives by [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. For $v:K\to L$, the two sides of $\rho_L j_E(v)=j_M(T_{M/E}v)\rho_K$ have representative $T_{M/E}v$. The shifted-map formula in the calculus gives
$$\rho_K[1]=j_M(\sigma_{M/E,K})\rho_{K[1]}.$$
Indeed the left side has representative $\sigma_{M/E,K}$, as does the right side, using the normalized identity transition of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. This gives natural vertex comparisons compatible with the specified shifts.

source.place: Transport isomorphisms used in TR2--TR4 and final exact identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-distinguished-diagram-lifting] to any finite configuration of distinguished rows used below, together with the additional arrows and equations under consideration. Its hypotheses are the finite-stage structures of step 2. The lifted vertices are $X_M=T_{M/E_X}K_X$; a third map with representative $p_M:Z_M\to T_{M/E_X}(K_X[1])$ becomes $\sigma_{M/E_X,K_X}p_M:Z_M\to X_M[1]$. All repeated vertices have the same lift, all selected rows are distinguished, and the stated equations hold at that stage. On mapping a stage row back, the third map is multiplied by $\sigma^{-1}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones], cancelling this correction; step 3 restores the original vertices. Common-stage composition and the shifted-map formula of [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] therefore recover exactly the original equations.

source.place: TR2--TR4 common-stage representation; auxiliary lifting assertion separated from the axiom checks.

proof.text: For TR1, represent a given f=[M,u] at M and use finite-stage TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to choose a cone triangle of u. The second and third maps, and the object comparisons of step 3, are precisely the common-stage cone triangle in [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones], whose first map is the original f. For (E,K), the finite-stage identity triangle K to K to 0 to K[1] supplies its identity triangle. The object (E,0) is zero in P_T: every common-stage Hom to or from it is zero, since additive scalar extension preserves zero objects, so the class of every such map is zero. Distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism because composing the witness triangle isomorphisms again gives a witness.

source.place: Proof, TR1 sentence, including the zero object and identity triangle.

proof.text: For TR2, a distinguished triangle Delta lifts by step 4 to a distinguished triangle at M. Its signed rotation is distinguished by finite-stage TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], and maps to the signed rotation of Delta: addition preserves the minus sign and sigma identifies the shifted first arrow with the formula in [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Therefore the signed rotation is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Conversely, write Delta=(X,Y,Z,f,i,p) and suppose its rotation (Y,Z,X[1],i,p,-f[1]) is distinguished. In step 4 include Delta itself as additional vertices and arrows, and include the equations identifying the rotated arrows with i,p,-f[1]. At M identify the lifted X[1] with X_M[1] using sigma. The shifted-map formula in the calculus and naturality of sigma in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] then make the lifted distinguished row exactly (Y_M,Z_M,X_M[1],i_M,p_M,-f_M[1]), where p_M now denotes the corrected last arrow of Delta as in step 4. The reverse implication of finite-stage TR2 makes (X_M,Y_M,Z_M,f_M,i_M,p_M) distinguished. Its common-stage image is isomorphic to Delta by the vertex comparisons of step 3, so Delta is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. This proves both implications without assuming that a stage inclusion reflects distinguishedness.

source.place: Proof, TR2 sentence; reverse implication via inverse signed rotation.

proof.text: For TR3, write the rows as X to Y to C to X[1] and X' to Y' to C' to X'[1], with first maps f,f', and let a:X to X', b:Y to Y' satisfy bf=f'a. Apply step 4 including these two maps and this equality. At the resulting stage M both rows are distinguished and b_M f_M=f'_M a_M holds, not merely its image in P_T. Finite-stage TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] supplies c_M with c_M i_M=i'_M b_M and a_M[1] p_M=p'_M c_M. Its image, restored through the vertex comparisons, supplies c:C to C'. Since [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] computes composition at a common stage and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] respects the shifts, the two displayed equations become c i=i' b and a[1]p=p'c in P_T. These are precisely the other two equations in [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], so the given square extends with its original a,b.

source.place: Proof, TR3 sentence; all square and triangle equations at one stage.

proof.text: For TR4 let f:X to Y and g:Y to Z be composable and take any distinguished cone triangles (X,Y,C_f,f,i_f,p_f), (X,Z,C_{gf},gf,i_{gf},p_{gf}) and (Y,Z,C_g,g,i_g,p_g). Apply step 4 to all three triangles, f,g and their composite equation. They become distinguished cone triangles at the same stage with exactly the same first and second vertices wherever those are shared. Finite-stage TR4 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives maps alpha_M:C_f to C_{gf}, beta_M:C_{gf} to C_g and the distinguished triangle with last map i_f[1] p_g. At M the face equations are alpha_M i_f=i_{gf}g, p_{gf}alpha_M=p_f, beta_M i_{gf}=i_g, and p_g beta_M=f[1]p_{gf}. Map the entire finite diagram back to P_T. The calculus preserves its four equations, and the shift comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] identifies the last map with the actual composite i_f[1]p_g. The remaining cone triangle is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Thus the octahedron is obtained for the given cones, not just for newly chosen ones; the representative and cone choices used for the witnesses are interchangeable by [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence], while the lifting lemma retains the prescribed original rows. The four verified axioms with the additive shift of step 3 now give an ordinary triangulated category by [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Proof, TR4 sentence and the triangulated-category consequence; arbitrary prescribed cone triangles.

proof.text: For exactness of j_E, take any distinguished triangle at E. Its image with the shift comparison is a common-stage cone triangle (choose M=E and its first arrow), hence is distinguished by [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. Additivity and the natural shift comparison are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], so this is exactness in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For E contained in F, the natural isomorphism rho_{F/E}:j_E to j_F T_{F/E} from step 3 is compatible with the shift structures: at K the equation is rho_K[1]=j_F(sigma_{F/E,K}) rho_{K[1]}. Both sides were explicitly represented over F in step 3. Inverting rho gives the orientation j_F T_{F/E} isomorphic to j_E requested in the statement. The inverse equation remains shift compatible, and [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] makes T_{F/E} exact. Hence these are natural isomorphisms of exact functors, with the specified comparisons, rather than mere natural isomorphisms of their underlying functors.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: exact stage inclusions and exact natural isomorphisms.

The item's statement matches the blueprint word for word and is not weakened. The coefficient category is the raw scalar localization Dbc(T,O_E)[1/ϖ] over the completed sheaf A_T, with no Karoubi envelope and no identification with the constant sheaf. Step checks: step 1 applies the linear derived-category Mathlib leaf to the ordinary ring O_E acting through constant sections. Step 2 uses the uniform-complete triangulation lemma and scalar localization with R=O_E under the same hypotheses on T. In step 3 I checked by hand that the representative of ρ_K[1] is σ_{M/E,K}, because σ_{M/M}=id follows from T_{M/M}=id and compatibility with the associators. For TR1, (E,0) is zero and the identity triangle comes from stage E. For the converse of TR2, (id,id,σ_X) is a triangle isomorphism from the lifted rotation row to the rotation of (X_M,Y_M,Z_M,f_M,i_M,σp_M), so no reflection of distinguishedness by j_M is assumed. For TR3, the σ correction cancels and a[1]p=p'c holds with the original a and b. For TR4, the face equations and the last map i_f[1]p_g agree with the Mathlib Octahedron, and the composite equation is lifted. For step 9, the CommShift condition for ρ is the equation of step 3. The new node lem-weil-pbc-distinguished-diagram-lifting is true: lift the witness isomorphisms with their inverse and triangle equations, move the cone row to the larger stage by exactness of the transition functor, and apply finite-stage TR1. I tested it on empty data, no marked rows, repeated vertices, X[1] occurring as a vertex, and zero and identity arrows. It is strictly between the common-stage calculus and the item and is not a relabelling. I found no duplicate by rg over dag/nodes and checks of cone-independence, the common-stage cones, idempotent-complete triangulation, thm-coef-qbar-verdier and the chunk approximation lemma. It now names the scalar-localization structure of lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated on Dbc(T,O_E)[1/ϖ] of def-weil-pbc-rational-category, the one in which the common-stage cones are chosen, and both ids are added to stmt_deps. I also added the missing merged_into and lean_audit fields and put blueprint right after id. blueprint_update.statement:
The shift and distinguished triangles of [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]
satisfy the four Verdier axioms:

1. every morphism has a distinguished cone triangle, the identity triangle
   is distinguished, and distinguishedness is closed under isomorphism;
2. a triangle is distinguished if and only if its signed rotation is
   distinguished;
3. every commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
   triangles extends to a morphism of triangles;
4. cone triangles for composable maps can be placed in an octahedral diagram
   whose required faces commute and whose remaining cone triangle is
   distinguished.

Consequently $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated category. Every
finite-stage inclusion $j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ is exact, and
the identifications $j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms.

proof.text:
TR1: every morphism has a cone triangle by
[def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]; the identity triangle is the cone
triangle of an identity (cone zero), and distinguishedness is closed under
isomorphism by the definition. TR2: by
[prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] a distinguished triangle and its
signed rotation may be represented over one common finite field, so the
finite-stage TR2 axiom makes the signed rotation distinguished (the shift in
the signed rotation being the $\sigma$-comparison of the definition). TR3:
given a commutative square between the first arrows of two distinguished
triangles, represent the two triangles over one common finite field (using
the transport isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]) and apply the finite-stage TR3
axiom; the resulting vertical arrow transports back to $\mathcal P_T$. TR4:
the same common-stage representation of two composable morphisms, together
with the cone independence of [prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence], and the
finite-stage TR4 axiom produce the octahedral diagram whose remaining cone
triangle is distinguished. Hence $\mathcal P_T$ is an ordinary triangulated
category; $j_E$ is exact because cone triangles of $j_E(f)$ are the
corresponding common-stage cone triangles, and the identifications
$j_FT_{F/E}\simeq j_E$ are exact natural isomorphisms by
[prop-weil-pbc-cone-independence].
